scenes.narration: Wonder Woman's Lasso of Truth has a real origin. Not from an island of Amazons, but from a psychology lab at Harvard.
scenes.image_credit: Ilustración propia generada con IA (lazo y baumanómetro; sin personaje ni arte de DC).

scenes.narration: Her creator, William Moulton Marston, held three Harvard degrees, one a PhD in psychology. In Hugo Münsterberg's lab he studied one question: what happens to blood pressure when someone lies?
scenes.image_credit: Hugo Münsterberg Psychologe. Unknown authorUnknown author, Public domain. Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hugo_M%C3%BCnsterberg_Psychologe.jpg

scenes.narration: The clue came from his wife, Elizabeth Holloway, a lawyer and psychologist: she noticed that when she got mad or excited, her blood pressure seemed to climb. Together they published studies on systolic pressure.
scenes.image_credit: William Moulton Marston and Elizabeth Holloway Marston. Photo courtesy of Moulton "Pete" Marston, Public domain. Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:William_Moulton_Marston_and_Elizabeth_Holloway_Marston.png

scenes.narration: Marston took readings with an ordinary blood-pressure cuff, at intervals. In 1921, in Berkeley, police officer John Larson built on that idea to make the first continuous-recording polygraph, and later Leonarde Keeler made it portable. So Marston didn't invent it alone.
scenes.image_credit: The Ink polygraph Wellcome L0004447. autor en Commons, CC BY 4.0. Wellcome Collection vía Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Ink_polygraph_Wellcome_L0004447.jpg

scenes.narration: In 1923, a Washington court rejected the results of this kind of test in the Frye case: it lacked general acceptance among experts. Even Larson distrusted its error rate.
scenes.image_credit: Lie detector test. Ed Westcott, Public domain. Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lie_detector_test.jpg

capa.etiqueta: Frye case: test rejected in court

scenes.narration: In 1941, under the pen name Charles Moulton, he created Wonder Woman, with a golden lasso that compels the truth. And her bracelets, he said, came from the ones worn by Olive Byrne, his former student, who lived with him and Elizabeth. Would you trust a lasso more than a polygraph?
scenes.image_credit: William Marston Aug 1922 newspaper photo. The Morning Tulsa daily world, Public domain. Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:William_Marston_Aug_1922_newspaper_photo.jpg
